reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling, Virginia campus publishes 38 MW of IT capacity across 700,000 square feet of technical space, ranking 13th among the 25 Virginia facilities that disclose a capacity figure.

The disclosure gap is the larger fact. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, and only 25 of them publish a capacity number. Those 25 account for 1,603 MW in total, of which Sterling is 2.4 percent. Any statewide account of AI load in Virginia therefore rests on a small, self-selected slice of the fleet, and Sterling's 38 MW sits mid-scale within that slice.

At an assumed 40 kW per rack, 38 MW supports roughly 950 racks. That is an assumption about possible scale, not a published specification. The facility lists no certifications, so its qualification for any particular workload class is not stated. The data also carries no grid information and no announced expansion, which is the input the suitability score of 69 is missing. Whether Sterling can take on more AI load depends on facts this data does not contain.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
